canonical_data: A git-trackable vault of Markdown notes with YAML frontmatter, indexed by a fully rebuildable SQLite cache of full-text, embeddings, citations, and provenance links
current_repo_note: Candidate triage recorded 1,791 stars on 2026-08-25; this review's live check found 2,999, a fast-growing single-maintainer project at release v0.11.1. The Python package's `hyperresearch install` step places the `/hyperresearch` command into Claude Code, per the README's Install section, so the pipeline runs inside that host's sessions.
strengths: Verification battery (quote-integrity, retracted-citation, numeric-consistency, per-citation cite-check) gates every report before it ships
Persistent, rebuildable Markdown-plus-SQLite vault with graph, full-text, and semantic search that compounds across sessions
Eight scholarly-source integrations deduplicated into one client layer, plus open-access recovery for paywalled papers with disclosed provenance
Explicit prompt-injection handling: fetched web bodies are fenced as untrusted data across every read path
weaknesses: Its headline benchmark claim ('currently leads the DeepResearch-Bench RACE leaderboard') is internally benchmarked only; the README itself says third-party validation is pending
Provider-native to Anthropic models via Claude Code; the maintainer has not ported the subagent roster to other providers
Single-maintainer project at v0.11.x; no independent adoption signal beyond GitHub stars and forks yet
why_it_matters: Shows a deep-research pipeline that treats citation integrity and retraction-checking as hard gates rather than best-effort prompting, with a durable, human-readable vault instead of a one-shot report.
